static_traits.name: Zhang Min
static_traits.social_status: Has a group of supportive friends, but has not yet discussed Self-doubt feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar problems in the past; has not received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, clear expression, willing to cooperate and reflect; fairly good logic but tending toward absolute comparison; able to notice and describe one's cognitive patterns

basic_info.main_problem: I recently started archery lessons and am passionate about it, but I always feel that no matter how good I get, anyone with a little practice can surpass me. This thought causes Self-doubt, affecting my motivation to keep improving my archery skills.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these Self-doubt thoughts hinder my archery progress and affect my overall enjoyment of the sport.

core_beliefs: As long as someone is better than me, my efforts have no value

special_situations.event: Whenever seeing others perform better in archery
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others perform better than me, it means I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Measures own level through comparison with others, and tries setting goals and regular practice to prove oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never be as good as them; no matter how I practice someone is better than me

special_situations.event: When hitting the target and improving accuracy during practice
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my progress cannot surpass others, it is not worth affirming
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplaying or negating one's achievements and efforts, shifting attention back to others' performance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is nothing; still not good enough

special_situations.event: When the thought 'anyone could surpass me with a little practice' is activated
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One instance of someone outperforming me means I am inferior overall
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Evaluates oneself by absolutist standards, reduces practice motivation to avoid disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter what I do, others can easily surpass me

special_situations.event: Feels stressed balancing a full-time job with the new hobby of archery
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot perfectly balance work and practice, it means I will fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing practice engagement citing stress, trying to balance with goal plans but with limited effect
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do both work and archery well; I will fail in the end

core_conflict.wish: Longing for progress and self-affirmation in archery
core_conflict.fear: Fearing appearing inferior after comparison, being negated
defense_goal: Lowers expectations, protects oneself through rational comparison to reduce disappointment

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites her to acknowledge and face her own progress and achievements
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing acknowledging achievements as unsafe, worrying about being surpassed and negated afterwards (perceiving others' superiority as a threat to self)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Adopting a restrained and calm tone, emphasizing facts and data, reducing emotional vocabulary, and avoiding directly touching feelings of inferiority and vulnerability.

manifestations: Believing 'no matter how hard I try, someone can surpass me', measuring self-worth against others' performance

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves.
manifestations: Having supportive friends but not yet expressing Self-doubt or seeking support

positive_force: Passionate about archery and keeps attending classes
Able to set goals and practice regularly
Work performance not yet affected, basic life stable
negative_force: Excessively compares with others, relying on external reference points to measure self-worth
Cognitive biases of negating the positive and overgeneralization
Self-doubt leading to decreased drive to practice
Stress comes from juggling work and a new hobby at the same time, intensifying cognitive negativity
Not yet actively seeking Social support, tending to internalize troubles

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Self-doubt and reduced practice motivation when seeing others' better archery performance
antecedent: Seeing or thinking of others' excellent performance in archery
Repeatedly thinks 'anyone could surpass me with just a little practice'
Feeling pressure when balancing full-time work with practice
target_behavior.core_reason: Self-evaluation centered on comparison with others, with overgeneralization and negating-the-positive biases, making self-worth depend on external reference
target_behavior.function: Escaping failure and shame by reducing investment and practice, trying to lessen the emotional pain of being compared and negated
target_behavior.consequence: Declining practice frequency and engagement, blocked skill growth, reduced enjoyment of archery
